_comment: R7.2. Villagers standing in the square, placed by scripts/world/village_npcs.gd the same way opening.json places the opening's cast: data describes, code places. `config_key` names a block in data/config/art.json (a tint on Grandpa's or the trainer's rig, never KayKit's Ranger — see art.json's own comment on those keys). `greeting` names a conversation id in data/dialogue/village.json; the prompt label is always "Greet <name>", built by the placer rather than stored here, so it can never accidentally contain "talk" or "choose" — tests/smoke_opening.gd finds Grandpa and the starters by exactly those substrings.
_comment_greeting_when: OF30. `greeting` is what a villager says by default and never stops being that. `greeting_when` is an OPTIONAL, ORDERED list of branches checked ahead of it, each `{ if_flag | unless_flag, conversation }` against autoload/progression_state.gd -- first match wins, no match falls through to `greeting`. Deliberately additive: a villager who gains a role gains a list entry, and nobody's greeting is ever replaced (D39's dual-role rule -- SC12 adds Tam's battle offer as a THIRD entry here, and OF31 gives Mira and Oskar their own lists, without touching this one). Either key may hold a single flag id or an array of them, all of which must hold. No `and`/`or`/`not` beyond that, and no nesting: this is a lookup table, not a quest engine (spec sec19 bans one, and progression_state.gd's own header says so twice).
_comment_sc12_sc13: SC12/SC13. Mira, Oskar and Tam are the Meadows' three Band-1 trainers (spec sec3, D39's dual-role rule made real): once each one's vendor/gift branch has actually been spent, greeting them again offers a CHALLENGE conversation instead -- and keeps offering it, every greeting, for as long as their defeat flag (`defeated_mira`/`defeated_oskar`/`defeated_tam`, encounter_director.gd's SB9 write) is unset. The challenge's last line carries `battle:<trainer_id>` (sequence_director.gd), the same fight `data/config/trainers.json`'s matching `placed_by: "village_npcs"` entry runs. Once beaten, a `_beaten` conversation takes over as their permanent steady state and is inserted ABOVE their old standing vendor branch -- Mira's and Oskar's `_beaten` lines carry the exact same `shop:`/`shop:creatures:` effect their old standing branch always did, so the store/swap stays reachable forever even though the old branch entry below it is now unreachable in practice (kept verbatim rather than deleted, per D39: a vendor branch is never rewritten, only superseded). Tam has no such branch to carry -- his gifts are one-time and both already spent by the time he is challengeable -- so his `_beaten` line is flavour only.
_comment_positions: World metres, on the village square flat (data/config/terrain_playground.json's `flats`, centre [10,-10], radius 18). Chosen and checked against the real runtime structure colliders and the square's four dirt paths (data/config/terrain_playground.json's `paths.routes`, all of which start at [10,-10]) with a headless probe — every position clears every building footprint and every path's 3m width + 1.5m shoulder by several metres, and all three sit far short of Grandpa's house/door/outside markers (~-16,-15 to -9.7,-15), well clear of the smoke test's walked lanes there. `facing_deg` points each villager at the well so the square reads as people gathered around it; `npc_body.gd` turns them to face the player on approach regardless. AMENDED BY OF31: Mira no longer stands in the square at all -- the merchant has a shop, so she is inside cottage_a behind her counter (see her own `_why`). The probe's clearances above still describe the other four.

hair._comment: Iron grey, distinct from farmer (#5c3a22), smith (#8a8578), ranger (#7a3c22) and Bryn (#c9a86a) so the sixth body on this rig does not read as one of the others wandered north out of the square.

Facing 215 degrees turns her back toward the square, so she is looking at whoever walks up from the well.

greeting_when._why: FIRST in the list: once the tournament is won, every branch below it is spent and this is her permanent steady state. It is also the line the owner directive asks for -- the one that says a Meadowhart can be ridden and what the saddle costs. The pattern itself is granted by the final round's own `reward.flags`, not by this conversation, so a champion who never walks back here still has it.

Round 3. Ends on `battle:tournament_final_oskar`, and stays offered for as long as the final is unwon -- which is what makes a loss retryable: nothing is consumed by losing, so the player heals their team and greets her again.
Round 2. Ends on `battle:tournament_semi_tam`.
Round 1. Ends on `battle:tournament_quarter_mira`.

FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. Halda's first interaction is the explicit registration briefing, and its effect writes the controller-facing opening:tournament_registered handoff only when the player has actually read the requirements. It sits below active-bracket branches and above every readiness branch, so a late-game player is never sent backward into onboarding.

FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD sign-up. The complete five-creature team, strength and volatile rested/fed/happy state still come from tournament.gd. `home_built` is the save-compatible compact Camp requirement owned by home_progress; `creature_bed_built` proves a real physical bed; `player_slept_at_home` proves the player actually rested/recovered at camp. No Workbench or house architecture flag is required. The conversation's last line sets `tournament_entered`.

FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. A ready five-creature team without the camp/bed/recovery proof gets one concrete next step instead of falling back to generic banter. This branch is below sign-up and above the ordinary condition branch, so it never interrupts an entered bracket.

RG19-spec/D68. Trained, but not in shape: the owner's own entry rule is that entrants are 'well rested, well fed, and happy'. Told as a reason rather than a locked door -- the line names rest, food and care, and the team screen shows which creature is short of which. Sits ABOVE the train branch so a team that is levelled but hungry hears about the food rather than about levels, and below sign-up so a ready team never sees it. `unless_flag` includes `tournament_entered` so a player who has already signed up is never sent back out to feed somebody mid-bracket.
You have the bodies, they are not ready. Told as a reason rather than as a locked door -- she names what to go and do, which is the whole difference between an entry condition and a wall.
After registration, the team-size reminder. The threshold is tournament.json's five-creature cap-aligned value; the dialogue says five rather than carrying a second gameplay number.

_comment_tournament_1: TOURNAMENT-1. Halda, the tournament marshal, is the seventh entry and the first villager whose whole `greeting_when` list is a progression LADDER rather than a vendor/gift pair. That is deliberately the existing mechanism and not a new one: the tournament has seven states and each of them is one flag, so the ordered-branch reader `village_npcs.greeting_for()` already written for Mira answers all seven without a line of new code. Order matters and is checked by tests/test_tournament.gd -- champion first, then the rounds newest-first, then sign-up, then the two not-ready explanations.
_comment_t1_creature_rig: T1-CREATURE-RIG, 2026-08-30. Placed 12 of the 15 civilian bodies T3-INSTALL generated, rigged, animated and installed at assets/characters/<slug>/ but never stood up anywhere (docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md's T3-INSTALL entry calls this 'the single largest remaining install opportunity in the game').
